title: OpenWarrant Format 1.0: shared definitions
description: Hand-written and normative for docs/format/FORMAT-1.0.md. Where this schema and the prose of FORMAT-1.0.md disagree, the prose wins and this schema is the defect. Lexical shapes shared by the other Format 1.0 schemas; it validates no document on its own. Byte limits in the prose (ids 64 bytes, titles 120 bytes, summaries 200 bytes) are bytes of UTF-8; JSON Schema `maxLength` counts code points, so where a value may be non-ASCII the bound here is necessary, not sufficient.

word.description: Appendix A `word`: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

dotted.description: Appendix A `dotted`, section 7.1: an extension name, two or more labels joined by `.`.

name.description: Appendix A `name`: a word or a dotted name.

recordId.description: Section 5 and Appendix A `record-id`: an uppercase letter, then uppercase letters or digits, then one or more groups of `-` and letters or digits; at most 64 bytes (`REQ-pr1`, `OBL-001`, `S-intent`).

sectionId.description: Section 3.4: `S-` and the slug of a section's name.

itemId.description: Section 5 and Appendix A `item-id`: `i-` and lowercase hex.

alias.description: Appendix A `alias`: a record-id shaped alias (`OW-WAR-0146`) or `t-` and hex (`t-0d61d`).

uuidv7.description: Section 5: a work document's `uuid` is a UUIDv7 (RFC 9562): version nibble 7, variant 10xx. The prose does not fix the case of the hex digits; both are admitted here.

ref.description: Appendix A `ref`: a record id, `<alias>/<record-id or item-id>`, an alias, `war://<uuid>`, or `md:<path>#<slug>`. Appendix A gives `doc:<path>` (section 5) no place in a relation target.

globalId.description: Section 5: a global id as the model carries it: a record id, an alias (a work document's own record), `<alias>/<id>`, `md:<file>#<slug>`, `doc:<path>`, or `war://<uuid>`.

legacyId.description: Section 12: an id a legacy store gives and the model carries unrenamed. A directory Warrant's milestone, `<alias>/M1` or `<alias>/MB` (an uppercase letter, then uppercase letters or digits, with no `-` group), and a SAS section or subsection, `WAR-SAS-101.1` (a record id with dotted numbers). No Format 1.0 document authors one.

modelId.description: An id as the model and a context packet carry it: a global id (section 5), or a legacy store's id lowered unrenamed (section 12).

coreRelationKind.description: Section 3.6: the closed set of core relation kinds.

relationKind.description: Section 3.6: a core kind, or a dotted extension kind (carried and inert). Any other kind is refused (`format.relation-kind`).

legacyRelationKind.description: Section 12: a relation kind a legacy store gives and the model carries unrenamed, beside the core and dotted kinds: a directory Warrant's `[[roadmap]]` (`roadmap`) and `[[parents]]` (`parent`), and a promoted ticket's `promoted_to`. No Format 1.0 document authors one; an authored one is refused (`format.relation-kind`).

modelRelationKind.description: A relation kind as the model carries it: a core or dotted kind (section 3.6), or a legacy store's kind (section 12).

gateUri.description: Appendix A `gate-uri`: `gate://<gate-id>@<semver>`. Appendix A does not define `gate-id`; the shape here (lowercase labels joined by `.`, `_` or `-`) is the one every example uses.

line.description: One line: no LF and no CR.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 date-time with an explicit offset.

stringList.description: A flat frontmatter list (section 3.2): an array of scalars.

fieldValue.description: Section 8 `fields`: a string, or an array of strings for a frontmatter list.
